earlier_scan.note: Burate (Geelvink Bay) has only a Clouse 1992 wordlist and Jones 1987 survey; no phonology or grammar exists.

new_statements.quote: Sedangkan bahasa-bahasa yang dikelompokkan ke dalam keluarga bahasa Geelvink Bay adalah bahasa-bahasa Papua yang berada di wilayah bagian barat dari daratan Mamberamo ke wilayah Waropen, dan beberapa bagian di wilayah Nabire dan Pulau Yapen. Bahasa-bahasa seperti bahasa Kirikiri, Demisa, Fayu, Iau, Biritai, Burate, Awera, Tarunggare, Onate, dan lain-lain masuk dalam keluarga bahasa ini. [...] Bahasa-bahasa ini hampir merupakan bahasa bunyi (tonal languages) yang sistem morfologinya tidak serumit bahasa-bahasa Trans New Guinea, tetapi mempunyai sistem fonologi suprasegmetal yang sangat rumit, yaitu sistem bunyi (tone)nya berkisar antara 3 sampai 9 tone.
new_statements.translation: The languages grouped into the Geelvink Bay family are Papuan languages located in the area west of the Mamberamo mainland over to the Waropen area, and some parts of the Nabire area and Yapen Island. Languages such as Kirikiri, Demisa, Fayu, Iau, Biritai, Burate, Awera, Tarunggare, Onate, and others belong to this family. [...] These languages are nearly [all] tone languages (tonal languages), whose morphological systems are not as complex as those of the Trans New Guinea languages, but which have a very complex suprasegmental phonological system, i.e. their tone systems range from 3 to 9 tones.
new_statements.citation: Sawaki, Yusuf Willem. 2018. Meneropong tipologi bahasa-bahasa di Papua: suatu tinjuan singkat [Looking at the typology of the languages of Papua: a brief review]. Linguistik Indonesia 36(2): 129-143. doi:10.26499/li.v36i2.79. (CELD-UNIPA Manokwari)

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Sawaki 2018 exists and is open: A's saved landing page (work dir) carries citation_title 'MENEROPONG TIPOLOGI BAHASA-BAHASA DI PAPUA: SUATU TINJUAN SINGKAT', citation_doi 10.26499/li.v36i2.79 and citation_pdf_url = A's URL; the mirror PDF is a 15-page text-layer PDF (594 KB) with matching header 'Linguistik Indonesia, Agustus 2018, 129-143, Volume ke-36, No. 2', author Yusuf Sawaki, CELD & Universitas Papua. Quote checked in : the first segment (family membership list naming Burate) is verbatim at lines 137-141 (p.131) and the second segment ('Bahasa-bahasa ini hampir merupakan bahasa bunyi (tonal languages).. berkisar antara 3 sampai 9 tone.') is verbatim at lines 159-162 (top of p.132); A…
new_statements.relation_note: p.131-132 group-level 'nearly all tonal, 3-9 tones' for a 'Geelvink Bay' grouping that names Burate; p.133 Papua-wide 'penultimate and final word stress'; p.133-134 Lakes Plain tone (Clouse 1993). No Burate data anywhere in the paper.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Group-level, hedged claim: the languages the author files under 'Geelvink Bay' (a list that includes Burate but also the Lakes Plain languages) are 'nearly [all]' tonal with 3-9 tones; separately, languages of Papua 'in general' have penultimate and final word stress. Nothing is asserted of Burate individually.
new_statements.exceptions: 'hampir' (nearly/almost) hedges the tonal claim; no languages singled out
new_statements.identity_note: A Papua-wide typological overview (15 pp., in Indonesian). Burate is named once (p.131) in a membership list of the author's 'Geelvink Bay' family, which conflates East Geelvink Bay proper (Demisa, Burate, Awera, Tarunggare) with Lakes Plain languages (Kirikiri, Fayu, Iau, Biritai); the tonal generalisation that follows (p.131-132) is group-level and evidently rests on the Lakes Plain literature (p.133-134 cites Clouse 1993:19 for western Lakes Plain tone). No Burate data, no Burate-specific statement; not a first-hand description of this languoid.
